Mythic: the imps take revenge on the larger demons by stealing from their hoards.
Seat, master and history are Living Server lore.

story:
The imps steal from the great demons of the court, and something has to happen to what they steal. Most of it goes to Marquis Scottiax. He is a marquis of High Lord Baelerdoth's household, with a seat between Baelerdoth's hall and Oro's, and for ten Rolls he has been the fence for the bottom of the Roll: he buys from the imps what they cannot keep, Duke Aypol's green and blue and white metal, the hoard-pieces of dukes and earls, once the cushion of the Queen's chair, and he pays them in the one thing imps want, which is to be left alone. A demon under his protection is not stepped on. He is the richest marquis in the court and the only peer the imps call friend.

He came to it by being robbed himself. In the Second Roll the imps took his whole hoard in a night, and instead of going to the Chancellor, as Aypol later did, Scottiax went down to the bottom of the Roll and asked the imps what they wanted for it back. They had never been asked before. He paid, and they returned it, and he asked them what else they had. By the Fourth Roll he was buying everything they took.

Aypol has asked the Chancellor many times to strike Scottiax off for receiving the court's own metal. Adremal has ruled every time that a marquis who buys is not a marquis who falls. When the imps set up their seal stalls in the realms' entrance halls after the doors opened, the court noticed that their stock was very good and very large, and that Scottiax had supplied it. Mystemas, who knows everything the imps know, says Scottiax is the only demon on the Roll he would not sell out, because Scottiax would buy him first.
legend: Scottiax stands between High Lord Oro's hall and Baelerdoth's in the east, a little apart from both, with East Ward camps not far off. Level 73, no script. Pull him out toward open ground, away from the Ward camps and from Duke Bimure. Players say he is the demon the imps sell their loot to, which is why the seal merchants are so well stocked, and that he is the only big demon the imps cheer for. His drops are ordinary. The imps' prices are not. Kill him where you pulled him to: drift back between the halls and you are fighting a Ward camp as well. Some Midgard groups swear the seal merchants raise their prices the day after he dies.

loremasterTopic.text: A marquis of High Lord [Baelerdoth]'s household and the fence of the court, who buys what the imps steal and pays them by keeping them from being stepped on. Duke [Aypol] wants him struck off; the imps call him friend.

bookPage: From the account book of an Albion merchant who traded at the imp stalls: The imp Kodo sold me a dented sapphire plate at a fair price and told me, unasked, where it came from. A knight of their court lost it to a fiend, the fiend lost it to a family of imps, the imps sold it to a marquis between the eastern halls, and the marquis sold it back to the stall. I asked why the marquis did not keep it. Kodo said the marquis never keeps anything; he only buys it, and that buying is a kind of keeping in that place, since a thing bought is a thing nobody else can steal.
